summary: This study investigates qubit error bursts in two Quantum Inspire transmon processors (Starmon-5 with Dolan junctions and Starmon-7 with Manhattan junctions) and reveals junction-specific signatures, including quasiparticle pumping in Dolan devices and an anomalous surge-and-suppression pattern in burst rate. Burst rates of $\gamma_\mathrm{kept} \approx 1.5$ and $1$ min$^{-1}$ are comparable to prior work after area normalization, with recovery times differing by $\times 8$ between devices ($t_\mathrm{rec} \sim 2$ ms versus $\sim 250$ µs).
motivation: Ionizing radiation–induced qubit error bursts limit quantum error correction performance in superconducting processors, motivating investigation of burst dynamics, recovery mechanisms, and mitigation strategies across nominally similar devices.
method: Mid-circuit measurement and template-matched filtering of simultaneous multi-qubit errors distinguish radiation-induced bursts from baseline $T_1$ and readout errors in two refrigerators; burst rate and duration are extracted as functions of cycle time and detection pulse rate.
result: Dolan-junction qubits show quasiparticle pumping: increasing π-pulse rate shortens $t_\mathrm{rec}$ by $\sim 4\times$ (from $\sim 2$ ms to $\sim 500$ µs) via a built-in trap, absent in Manhattan junctions; separately, Starmon-5 exhibits an anomalous surge with $\gamma_\mathrm{kept}$ rising by $\times 10$–$\times 100$ after 1–4 weeks at base temperature, then suppressing to $\times 100$ below initial levels until thermal cycling.
